content:
This week saw contradictory reports exploring whether Apple has abandoned plans to launch a completely redesigned iPhone next year, which I'll tentatively call the 'iPhone 20 Pro'.

One analyst said Apple believes the task is too difficult, but Bloomberg immediately clarified that this is not the case, stating that the design will debut as scheduled in 2027. Today there's new evidence supporting the latter account……

Contradictory reports

Former Apple design chief Jony Ive often spoke about his long-term vision for the iPhone — to turn it into a single sheet of glass — and reportedly Apple remained very committed to this concept even after his departure.

We've already seen different theories about what this new device might be called. Some think it would have a standalone name, like the iPhone X and the rumoured iPhone Ultra. Others say it's simply next year's Pro model, so it would be called the iPhone 19 Pro. Still others say Apple would skip a generation and name it the iPhone 20 Pro to mark the device's 20th anniversary.

The story flared up again this week when an analyst at Jefferies said Apple had shelved the project, but Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said that wasn't the case. I've already shared my own view on what's actually going on.

iPhone 20 Pro surfaces in supply chain

Chinese leaker 'Digital Chat Station' (DCS) has now joined the fray, saying he has seen the device's display in Apple's supply chain, and it matches our expectations.

We expect Apple to use more sophisticated optical processing, similar to the Apple Watch display, creating the illusion of a screen that wraps around the edges of the body. Another leaker, Ice Universe, described the display like this:

DCS used very similar language to describe what they saw in the supply chain.

This further supports my view that while next year's design hasn't yet achieved the ultimate vision of a single sheet of glass, it represents a significant step in that direction.
